name: Delaware State University
colorsDescription: Red and Blue — bold and resolute, worn with pride on the Hornets' home turf in Dover.

stadium.name: Alumni Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Multi-purpose facility that also hosts track and field; one of the smallest FCS stadiums in the MEAC

sonic_profile.philosophy: We bring the thunder on every yard line — the Storm doesn't just play, it arrives.

teamWalk.name: The Hornet March
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the athletic complex to Alumni Stadium through campus, welcomed by fans and the sounds of the Approaching Storm.

tailgateCulture.name: The Dover Cookout
tailgateCulture.signatureFood: Crab dip and Old Bay chicken wings

signatureChants.name: STING EM
signatureChants.cue: After every score

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1891 as the Delaware College for Colored Students by the Delaware General Assembly, Delaware State University is one of the oldest HBCUs on the Eastern Seaboard. Located in Dover, the state capital, DSU made history in 2021 when it acquired Wesley College, becoming the first HBCU to acquire a non-HBCU institution.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as the Delaware College for Colored Students
Joined the MEAC as a founding member
First MEAC football championship under coach Bill Collick
MacKenzie Scott donates $20 million — largest single gift in school history
Acquires Wesley College, first HBCU to acquire a non-HBCU institution

funFacts: Delaware State was a founding member of the MEAC in 1971.
The university's Approaching Storm marching band is named for the energy they bring to every performance.
DSU's acquisition of Wesley College in 2021 added 40 acres and an entire college of health sciences.
The campus sits just minutes from Dover Speedway, home of the NASCAR Cup Series.
DeSean Jackson was named head football coach in 2024, bringing national attention to the program.

alumniRoster.name: DeSean Jackson
alumniRoster.role: NFL WR · Head Football Coach
alumniRoster.achievement: 3× Pro Bowl receiver, named DSU head football coach in 2024 to lead program rebuild.
alumniRoster.quote: Delaware State gave me a platform to give back.

alumniRoster.name: Bill Collick
alumniRoster.role: MEAC Coach of the Year · Athletic Director
alumniRoster.achievement: Led DSU to five MEAC championships over 12 seasons, compiled an 81-48 record.

name: Howard University
motto: Veritas et Utilitas — Truth and Service
colorsDescription: Navy and White — disciplined and distinguished, the colors of the Mecca since 1867.

stadium.name: William H. Greene Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Historic 1926 venue in the heart of Washington D.C.; expanded capacity to 10,000 for major games; home to one of HBCU football's most storied atmospheres

sonic_profile.philosophy: We are ambassadors of Howard University — the performance must match the prestige of The Mecca.

teamWalk.name: The Bison Walk
teamWalk.description: Players march from the Greene Athletics Complex through campus toward the stadium, flanked by students and alumni representing Howard's vast national alumni network.

signatureChants.name: REAL HU
signatureChants.cue: Called throughout the game — a response chant that echoes across the stadium

signatureChants.name: BISON CHARGE
signatureChants.lyrics: Charge! Let's go Bison, let's go!
signatureChants.cue: Offensive first down

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1867 and chartered by Congress, Howard University is one of the nation's most prestigious HBCUs and the only research university among them. Known as 'The Mecca,' Howard has produced Supreme Court justices, U.S. Vice Presidents, Nobel laureates, and generations of Black leaders. Its football program, established in 1893, is one of the oldest in HBCU athletics and made history in 2017 with the largest upset by point spread in college football history.

historicMilestones.event: Founded by an Act of Congress; named after Civil War general Oliver O. Howard
Football program established under director Charles Cook
Joined the MEAC as a founding member
Undefeated 11-0 season; Black College National Championship
Defeated UNLV 43-40 — largest point-spread upset in college football history

funFacts: Howard is the only HBCU chartered directly by the U.S. Congress.
The 2017 win over UNLV (as a 45.5-point underdog) is the largest upset by point spread in college football history.
The Showtime Marching Band performed at President Barack Obama's 56th Inaugural Parade.
Vice President Kamala Harris is a Howard alumna.
Howard's law school has produced more Black federal judges than any other law school in the country.

alumniRoster.name: Antoine Bethea
alumniRoster.role: NFL Safety · Super Bowl Champion · 3× Pro Bowl
alumniRoster.achievement: 14-year NFL career with the Colts, 49ers, Cardinals, and Giants. Won Super Bowl XLI with Indianapolis.
alumniRoster.quote: Howard prepared me for the real game — life.

alumniRoster.name: Kamala Harris
alumniRoster.role: 49th Vice President of the United States
alumniRoster.achievement: First woman, first Black American, and first person of South Asian descent to serve as U.S. Vice President.
alumniRoster.quote: Howard University is where I found my voice.

alumniRoster.name: Taraji P. Henson
alumniRoster.role: Golden Globe Winner · Oscar Nominee · Actress
alumniRoster.achievement: Star of Empire and Hidden Figures. Golden Globe winner and two-time Emmy nominee.
alumniRoster.quote: Howard is the Mecca — there's no place like it.

alumniRoster.name: Thurgood Marshall
alumniRoster.role: U.S. Supreme Court Justice · Civil Rights Pioneer
alumniRoster.achievement: First Black Supreme Court Justice. Argued Brown v. Board of Education before the Supreme Court.
alumniRoster.quote: None of us got where we are solely by pulling ourselves up by our bootstraps.

name: Morgan State University
motto: Growing the Future, Leading the World
colorsDescription: Blue and Orange — bold Baltimore pride, carried by the Bears since 1867.

stadium.name: Hughes Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Urban HBCU stadium in Baltimore's northeast corridor; adjacent to the Magnificent Marching Machine's legendary rehearsal fields

sonic_profile.philosophy: We don't just play music — we create an atmosphere that transforms sporting events into cultural celebrations.

teamWalk.name: The Bear Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk through campus to Hughes Stadium, cheered by students and Baltimore community members who have supported the program across generations.

tailgateCulture.name: Baltimore Bear Cookout
tailgateCulture.signatureFood: Old Bay steamed crabs and pit beef sandwiches

signatureChants.name: BEAR DOWN
signatureChants.cue: Third down defense, called by the student section

signatureChants.name: BLUE AND ORANGE
signatureChants.lyrics: Blue and orange all the way!
signatureChants.cue: After every score

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1867 as the Centenary Biblical Institute and renamed Morgan State University to honor the first chairman of its Board of Trustees, Morgan is Maryland's designated public urban university and the state's largest HBCU. The football program, begun in 1898, reached legendary status under coach Edward P. Hurt, who led the Bears to 14 CIAA championships between 1929 and 1959 and compiled the most dominant sustained record in HBCU football history.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as the Centenary Biblical Institute
Renamed Morgan State College after Reverend Lyttleton Morgan
Football team earns Black College National Championship under Earl Banks
Morgan State and Grambling play first American college football game outside the Western Hemisphere — in Tokyo, Japan
First MEAC Championship in 35 years under head coach Lee Hull

funFacts: Morgan State and Grambling played the first college football game outside the Western Hemisphere, in Tokyo, Japan in 1976.
The Magnificent Marching Machine has performed at Presidential Inaugurations, World Series games, and NFL Championship games.
The MMM made a cameo appearance in the film Head of State starring Chris Rock.
Morgan State has produced four Pro Football Hall of Famers — more than any MEAC school except SC State.
The MMM is heading to the 2026 Tournament of Roses Parade, one of the most prestigious global stages in music.

alumniRoster.name: Roosevelt 'Rosey' Brown
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 9× Pro Bowl OT
alumniRoster.achievement: Eight-time All-Pro tackle who anchored the New York Giants offensive line. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1975.

alumniRoster.name: Willie Lanier
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 8× Pro Bowl LB
alumniRoster.achievement: Kansas City Chiefs linebacker, nicknamed 'Contact.' Key member of the Super Bowl IV championship team. Hall of Fame, 1986.

alumniRoster.name: Kweisi Mfume
alumniRoster.role: U.S. Congressman · Former NAACP President
alumniRoster.achievement: Former President and CEO of the NAACP, currently serving as U.S. Representative for Maryland's 7th congressional district.
alumniRoster.quote: Morgan gave me the foundation to lead.

alumniRoster.name: David Satcher
alumniRoster.role: 16th U.S. Surgeon General
alumniRoster.achievement: Served as U.S. Surgeon General under President Clinton and as Director of the CDC.

name: Norfolk State University
colorsDescription: Green and Gold — the colors of Hampton Roads pride and Spartan tradition since 1935.

stadium.name: William 'Dick' Price Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: One of the largest on-campus FCS stadiums in the country; opened with a record crowd of 33,872 for the 1997 Labor Day Classic vs. Virginia State

sonic_profile.philosophy: The Legion doesn't just march — we command every inch of that field.

teamWalk.name: The Spartan March
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the athletic facility to Dick Price Stadium through campus, greeted by students and fans forming a tunnel of green and gold.

signatureChants.name: BEHOLD
signatureChants.cue: Student section opener, echoed throughout the stadium

signatureChants.name: S-P-A-R-T-A-N-S
signatureChants.cue: After every score

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1935 as the Norfolk Unit of Virginia Union University, Norfolk State became an independent institution in 1969 and achieved university status in 1979. The football program, begun in 1938, produced legendary coach Dick Price, who compiled the most wins in program history and led the Spartans to three consecutive CIAA championships (1974–76). Dick Price Stadium, opened in 1997, is one of the largest on-campus FCS venues in the country.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as the Norfolk Unit of Virginia Union University
Football program established
First of three consecutive CIAA championships under coach Dick Price
Dick Price Stadium opens; inaugural game draws record 33,872 fans
First and only MEAC Championship; first FCS playoff appearance

funFacts: Dick Price Stadium is one of the largest on-campus FCS football venues in the United States.
Coach Dick Price also led NSU's track team to two NCAA Division II national championships in 1973 and 1974.
The 2012 NSU basketball team famously upset #2 seed Missouri in the NCAA Tournament — a historic 15-over-2 upset.
Michael Vick was named Norfolk State's head football coach in 2024.
The Spartan Legion's 'Behold the Green and Gold' chant has been the signature sound of Dick Price Stadium since the stadium opened.

alumniRoster.name: Deon King
alumniRoster.role: 2015 Buck Buchanan Award Winner · LB
alumniRoster.achievement: Won the Buck Buchanan Award (FCS Defensive Player of the Year) in 2015 — the most prestigious individual award in FCS football.

alumniRoster.name: Dick Price
alumniRoster.role: Winningest Football Coach in NSU History
alumniRoster.achievement: Compiled a 62-41-4 record over 10 seasons; led NSU to 3 consecutive CIAA titles; 53 players went pro; stadium bears his name.

name: North Carolina Central University
colorsDescription: Maroon and Gray — regal and resolute, worn with pride in the Bull City since 1910.

stadium.name: O'Kelly-Riddick Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Named for campus steward Cadd G. O'Kelly, who cleared the land that became NCCU's first athletic field; hosted the 2023 HBCU National Championship celebration parade

sonic_profile.drumMajorStyle: High-energy showband style with commanding presence
sonic_profile.philosophy: We are the heartbeat of NCCU football — our electrifying performances bring the stadium to life and ignite the crowd.

teamWalk.name: The Eagle Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the athletic complex to O'Kelly-Riddick Stadium lined with students and community supporters. A Durham tradition beloved by multiple generations of Eagle fans.

tailgateCulture.name: The Bull City Cookout
tailgateCulture.signatureFood: Eastern NC pulled pork and sweet tea

signatureChants.name: EAGLE PRIDE
signatureChants.cue: After every score and throughout third quarter

signatureChants.name: AGGIE-EAGLE
signatureChants.cue: Called by the student section during defensive stands

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1910 by Dr. James E. Shepard as the National Religious Training School, NCCU became the first state-supported liberal arts college for Black Americans in 1923. Located in Durham, NC, the university is known for its nationally ranked law school, strong athletics, and the historic 1944 'Secret Game' in which NCCU's basketball team defeated a Duke Medical School squad in one of America's first integrated athletic competitions. The football program won the 2022 Celebration Bowl, claiming the HBCU National Championship.

historicMilestones.event: Founded by Dr. James E. Shepard as the National Religious Training School
Becomes the first state-supported liberal arts college for Black Americans
NCCU basketball team defeats Duke Medical School in the legendary 'Secret Game'
Joins MEAC as a founding member
Wins the Celebration Bowl 41-34 over Jackson State — HBCU National Champions

funFacts: NCCU won the 2022 HBCU National Championship in overtime on a 4th-and-goal stop against Deion Sanders' Jackson State.
The Sound Machine Marching Band performed at the North Carolina Governor's Inauguration in 1961 and at the Rose Bowl Stadium in 2023.
Herman Boone — the coach portrayed in Remember the Titans — is an NCCU alumnus.
André Leon Talley, legendary former editor of Vogue magazine, attended NCCU.
NCCU has posted eight or more wins in three consecutive seasons and has been one game from three straight MEAC titles.

alumniRoster.name: Doug Wilkerson
alumniRoster.role: NFL OG · 3× Pro Bowl
alumniRoster.achievement: Three-time Pro Bowl guard who anchored the San Diego Chargers offensive line through the AFC Championship era. Top AV all-time from NCCU.

alumniRoster.name: Herman Boone
alumniRoster.role: Football Coach · Civil Rights Symbol
alumniRoster.achievement: Head coach whose integration of the T.C. Williams High School team in 1971 was immortalized in the film Remember the Titans.
alumniRoster.quote: Football is just a sport. It's what you do off the field that defines you.

alumniRoster.name: André Leon Talley
alumniRoster.role: Editor-at-Large, Vogue Magazine
alumniRoster.achievement: One of the most influential figures in American fashion; served as Editor-at-Large of Vogue and creative director for American Vogue.

name: South Carolina State University
colorsDescription: Garnet and Blue — the colors of South Carolina pride and Bulldog dominance since 1896.

stadium.name: Oliver C. Dawson Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Exterior banners celebrate four Pro Football Hall of Famers; a Bulldog statue at the entrance is the most-photographed spot on campus on game day

sonic_profile.philosophy: The 101 has performed in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, The Rose Bowl, and NFL halftime shows — we carry the full weight of that legacy onto every field.

teamWalk.name: The Bulldog Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the ticket office area to the stadium locker room through fans and alumni — a pre-game ritual deeply embedded in Orangeburg's football culture.

tailgateCulture.name: Orangeburg Cookout
tailgateCulture.signatureFood: Duke's Bar-B-Que and sweet potato pie

signatureChants.name: BULLDOGS
signatureChants.lyrics: Go Bulldogs, go! Garnet and blue all the way!
signatureChants.cue: After every score and throughout the second half

signatureChants.name: FIFTH QUARTER
signatureChants.lyrics: We ain't done yet — fifth quarter!
signatureChants.cue: Post-game — when the Marching 101 and visiting band face off in a musical duel

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1896 as the Colored Normal, Industrial, Agricultural and Mechanical College of South Carolina, SC State is the state's only public HBCU. The football program is the most decorated in MEAC history, with a record 19 conference championships, four Pro Football Hall of Famers, and six Black College National Championships. The Marching 101, founded in 1918, is one of the most celebrated bands in HBCU culture. The campus also carries the memory of the 1968 Orangeburg Massacre, where three students were killed during a civil rights protest.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as Colored Normal, Industrial, Agricultural and Mechanical College of SC
Marching 101 band founded as a regimental band
The Orangeburg Massacre — three students killed during a civil rights protest on campus
Joins MEAC as a founding member
Historic NFL Draft class — eight players selected, most ever from SCSU
19th MEAC Championship, undefeated 5-0 in conference play

funFacts: SC State is the only school in South Carolina with four Pro Football Hall of Famers.
The program has produced 60 NFL Draft picks and 125 total NFL performers.
SC State players have participated in 22 of the 57 Super Bowls ever played.
The Marching 101 has performed at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the Rose Bowl Parade, and NFL halftime shows.
Coach Willie Jeffries became the first Black head coach at a predominantly white Division I-A football program when hired by Wichita State in 1979.

alumniRoster.name: Deacon Jones
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 'Secretary of Defense'
alumniRoster.achievement: Invented the quarterback sack. Two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1980.
alumniRoster.quote: You got to punish the quarterback.

alumniRoster.name: Donnie Shell
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 4— Super Bowl Champion
alumniRoster.achievement: Pittsburgh Steelers safety who won four Super Bowls. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2020.

alumniRoster.name: Harry Carson
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 9× Pro Bowl LB
alumniRoster.achievement: New York Giants linebacker and team captain of the 1986 Super Bowl XX championship team. Inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2006.
alumniRoster.quote: I played the game the right way.

alumniRoster.name: Javon Hargrave
alumniRoster.role: NFL DT · Current Player
alumniRoster.achievement: Third-round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2016. One of the most dominant interior defensive linemen of his era with the Eagles and 49ers.

name: Alcorn State University
colorsDescription: Purple and Gold — royalty and excellence, worn with pride since 1871.

stadium.name: Jack Spinks-Marino Casem Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Built in 1992 to replace historic Henderson Stadium; rededicated in 2011 to honor NFL pioneer Jack Spinks and legendary coach Marino Casem; record crowd of 26,500 witnessed Steve McNair break the NCAA total offense record in 1994

sonic_profile.philosophy: We don't just play music — we ignite the crowd and carry the spirit of every Brave who came before us.

teamWalk.name: The Brave Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the athletic complex through campus to the stadium, greeted by fans lining the path two hours before kickoff — a tradition dating back to the golden era of Coach Casem.

tailgateCulture.name: The Hilltop Cookout
tailgateCulture.signatureFood: Smoked catfish and sweet potato pie

signatureChants.name: BRAVELAND
signatureChants.cue: After every score, the student section leads the call

signatureChants.name: PURPLE REIGN
signatureChants.cue: Third quarter opener

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1871, Alcorn State University is the oldest public historically Black land-grant university in the United States. Named after Mississippi Governor James L. Alcorn, the university has produced civil rights icons, literary giants, and NFL legends from its hilltop campus in Lorman, Mississippi. The football program, begun in 1921, is one of the most decorated in HBCU history — claiming 13 SWAC championships, five Black College National Championships, and two College Football Hall of Famers in Marino Casem and Steve McNair.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as Alcorn University, the first HBCU land-grant institution in the U.S.
Football program established; inaugural season goes 4-0
Medgar Evers graduates and begins civil rights work; both Evers brothers played for the Braves
First of four Black College National Championships under coach Marino Casem
Steve McNair breaks NCAA career total offense record before 26,500 fans on The Hill
Steve McNair drafted 3rd overall by the Houston Oilers

funFacts: Alcorn State is the oldest public HBCU in the United States.
Steve McNair set a then-Division I-AA record with 16,823 career yards of total offense.
The Sounds of Dyn-O-Mite band has performed at every presidential inaugural parade since 1973.
Jack Spinks — the stadium's namesake — was the first Black Mississippian ever drafted by an NFL team, selected by the Pittsburgh Steelers in 1952.
Both Medgar Evers and his brother Charles played football for the Braves.
Alex Haley, author of Roots, served as a water boy for the Alcorn football team.

alumniRoster.name: Steve McNair
alumniRoster.role: NFL Co-MVP · 3× Pro Bowl QB · College Football Hall of Fame
alumniRoster.achievement: Set NCAA records at Alcorn before being drafted 3rd overall in 1995. Named NFL Co-MVP in 2003. Led Tennessee Titans to Super Bowl XXXIV.
alumniRoster.quote: Alcorn gave me the tools to compete at the highest level.

alumniRoster.name: Alex Haley
alumniRoster.role: Pulitzer Prize Winner · Author · Historian
alumniRoster.achievement: Author of Roots: The Saga of an American Family, which sparked a national conversation about African American history and identity.
alumniRoster.quote: In every conceivable manner, the family is link to our past.

alumniRoster.name: Medgar Evers
alumniRoster.role: NAACP Field Secretary · Civil Rights Martyr
alumniRoster.achievement: Legendary activist whose assassination in 1963 galvanized the Civil Rights Movement and helped dismantle Jim Crow in Mississippi.
alumniRoster.quote: You can kill a man but you can't kill an idea.

alumniRoster.name: Donald Driver
alumniRoster.role: NFL WR · 4× Pro Bowl · Super Bowl XLV Champion
alumniRoster.achievement: Green Bay Packers all-time leading receiver with 10,137 career yards. Won Super Bowl XLV after the 2010 season.

name: Grambling State University
colorsDescription: Black and Gold — power and prestige, carried by the Tigers since 1901 and recognized on every major stage in the world.

stadium.name: Eddie G. Robinson Memorial Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Named for legendary coach Eddie G. Robinson — the third-winningest coach in NCAA history. Features a dramatic 'GSU' and tiger-stripe graphic in the east grandstand; the adjacent Eddie G. Robinson Museum is a must-visit pilgrimage for any HBCU football fan

sonic_profile.philosophy: We are global ambassadors — from Super Bowl I to Tokyo to presidential inaugurations, the World Famed carries Grambling to every major stage on earth.

teamWalk.name: The Tiger Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk through campus to Eddie Robinson Stadium, greeted by fans in black and gold and the thunder of the World Famed Tiger Marching Band warming up in the distance.

signatureChants.name: WHO DAT TIGER
signatureChants.cue: After every score, echoed by the student section

signatureChants.name: BLACK AND GOLD
signatureChants.lyrics: Black and gold all the way, Tigers on display!
signatureChants.cue: Third quarter, band-led entrance

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1901 as the Colored Industrial and Agricultural School by Charles P. Adams in rural north Louisiana, Grambling State became the most famous small college in America under legendary coach Eddie Robinson, who compiled 408 victories in 57 seasons and became the first NCAA coach to reach 400 wins. The program has sent more than 200 players to the NFL, produced four Pro Football Hall of Famers, and played games on virtually every major stage in the world — from the Rose Bowl to Tokyo to Super Bowls I and II.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as the Colored Industrial and Agricultural School by Charles P. Adams
World Famed Tiger Marching Band founded with 17 instruments from Sears & Roebuck
Eddie Robinson begins 57-year coaching career
World Famed performs at Super Bowl I — first HBCU band on that stage
Grambling and Morgan State play first college football game outside the Western Hemisphere — in Tokyo, Japan
Eddie Robinson surpasses Bear Bryant to become winningest coach in college football history
Doug Williams becomes the first Black quarterback to win a Super Bowl, named Super Bowl XXII MVP

funFacts: Grambling has sent more than 200 players to the NFL — more than any school except Notre Dame at the program's peak.
The World Famed Tiger Marching Band performed at Super Bowls I, II, IX, and XXXII.
In 1976, Grambling and Morgan State played the first college football game held outside the Western Hemisphere, in Tokyo, Japan.
In 1985, Eddie Robinson surpassed Bear Bryant as the winningest coach in college football history.
Drake referenced the World Famed band by name in his 2015 hit 'Used To' featuring Lil Wayne.
The band appeared in the 2002 film Drumline and was featured in a Coca-Cola commercial dubbed 'The No. 1 Band in the Land.'

alumniRoster.name: Doug Williams
alumniRoster.role: Super Bowl XXII MVP · First Black QB to win a Super Bowl
alumniRoster.achievement: Led the Washington Redskins to a dominant Super Bowl XXII victory, throwing four touchdowns in the second quarter alone. Named the game's MVP.
alumniRoster.quote: Coach Robinson believed in me when nobody else did.

alumniRoster.name: Buck Buchanan
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · First HBCU player taken #1 overall
alumniRoster.achievement: Defensive tackle selected #1 overall in the 1963 AFL Draft by the Kansas City Chiefs. 8— AFL/AFC All-Star. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1990.

alumniRoster.name: Willie Davis
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 5— NFL Champion
alumniRoster.achievement: Defensive end for the Green Bay Packers dynasty under Vince Lombardi. Won five NFL championships including Super Bowls I and II. Hall of Fame, 1981.

alumniRoster.name: Erykah Badu
alumniRoster.role: Grammy Award Winner · Neo-Soul Pioneer
alumniRoster.achievement: One of the most influential musical artists of her generation. Attended Grambling before pursuing her music career.

name: Prairie View A&M University
motto: Preparing Students to Lead and Serve
colorsDescription: Purple and Gold — the colors of Texas royalty, worn by the Panthers since 1876 as the oldest public HBCU in the Lone Star State.

stadium.name: Panther Stadium at Blackshear Field
stadium.notableFeature: Built in 2016 on the footprint of the legendary Edward L. Blackshear Field; $60 million state-of-the-art facility with 10 luxury suites and an expandable capacity to 30,000; largely funded by alumni — students raised nearly two-thirds of construction costs

sonic_profile.drumMajorStyle: High-energy showband with dramatic field presence
sonic_profile.philosophy: We are the largest HBCU marching band in Texas — when the Storm rolls in, the whole stadium feels it.

teamWalk.name: The Panther Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk to Panther Stadium through campus lined by students and alumni, with the Marching Storm leading the procession in full uniform — a statement of community and pride every home Saturday.

signatureChants.name: P-V
signatureChants.cue: Initiated by the student section on every third down

signatureChants.name: PANTHER PRIDE
signatureChants.lyrics: Purple and gold, Panthers are bold!
signatureChants.cue: After every score

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1876 by the Texas Legislature as Alta Vista Agricultural College — the first public institution of higher education for Black Texans — Prairie View A&M is the oldest public HBCU in Texas and one of only two HBCUs in the Texas A&M University System. Under legendary coach Billy Nicks, the Panthers dominated HBCU football in the 1950s and early 1960s, winning five Black College National Championships. Today PVAMU is the largest HBCU in Texas and the third largest in the United States.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as Alta Vista Agricultural College — first public institution for Black Texans
Prairie View hosts the first Black college football bowl game in Texas history
First of five Black College National Championships under coach Billy Nicks
Ends a 0-80 losing streak — the longest in college football history — with a win over Langston
New $60 million Panther Stadium at Blackshear Field opens, replacing the legendary old stadium

funFacts: Prairie View A&M is the only charter member of the SWAC still in the conference today.
The Marching Storm performed at Super Bowl XLV halftime show and performed with Destiny's Child at a 2004 Dallas Cowboys game.
Prairie View holds the dubious record of the longest losing streak in college football history — 80 consecutive losses from 1989 to 1998.
The university's alumni raised nearly two-thirds of the $60 million needed to build the new Panther Stadium.
Coach Billy Nicks was so dominant in the 1950s that Eddie Robinson of Grambling reportedly dreaded playing Prairie View.

alumniRoster.name: Ken Houston
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 9× Pro Bowl Safety
alumniRoster.achievement: Intercepted 49 passes over a 14-year NFL career with the Houston Oilers and Washington Redskins. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1986.

alumniRoster.name: Otis Taylor
alumniRoster.role: Super Bowl IV Champion · 3× Pro Bowl WR
alumniRoster.achievement: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver who was a key weapon in Super Bowl IV. Recorded 410 catches for 7,306 yards over 10 seasons.

alumniRoster.name: Billy Nicks
alumniRoster.role: College Football Hall of Fame · 'Bear Bryant of Black College Football'
alumniRoster.achievement: Led Prairie View to five Black College National Championships and eight SWAC titles between 1945 and 1965. Career record of 127-39-8. Inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1999.

name: Southern University and A&M College
colorsDescription: Columbia Blue and Gold — the Baton Rouge sky and Louisiana sunshine, worn with championship pride since 1880.

stadium.name: A.W. Mumford Stadium
stadium.notableFeature: Largest on-campus stadium in the SWAC; opened in 1938 with WPA funds originally meant for a dormitory repurposed as a grandstand; the Human Jukebox occupies the west side stands and creates one of the most electric atmospheres in college football

sonic_profile.drumMajorStyle: Electrifying showmanship — the Jukebox sets the tempo for the entire stadium
sonic_profile.philosophy: We are the heartbeat of Southern University. When the Jukebox plays, Baton Rouge moves.

teamWalk.name: The Jaguar Walk
teamWalk.description: Players walk from the athletic facility to Mumford Stadium through a corridor of fans, family, and alumni — with the Human Jukebox setting the tone from the west stands as the team approaches.

signatureChants.name: JAGUARS
signatureChants.cue: After every score — called by the student section and echoed throughout Mumford

signatureChants.name: BLUE AND GOLD
signatureChants.lyrics: Blue and gold, that's our story — Southern U, all the glory!
signatureChants.cue: Third quarter opener led by the Jukebox

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1880 in New Orleans and relocated to Baton Rouge in 1914, Southern University is the largest HBCU in the United States and the flagship institution of the Southern University System — the only HBCU system in the country. The football program, established in 1916, is one of the most storied in HBCU history with 19 SWAC championships and nine Black College National Championships. A.W. Mumford Stadium, the largest on-campus stadium in the SWAC, has been the heart of Jaguar football since 1938.

historicMilestones.event: Founded in New Orleans by the Louisiana General Assembly
Relocated to Baton Rouge on the scenic bluffs above the Mississippi
Football program established
A.W. Mumford Stadium opens, built with WPA funds
Human Jukebox marching band founded by director T. Leroy Davis

funFacts: Southern University is the largest HBCU in the United States.
The Human Jukebox has performed at the Rose Parade, Presidential Inaugurations, and six Super Bowls.
The Bayou Classic against Grambling is played at the Superdome in New Orleans on Thanksgiving weekend and is the most attended HBCU football game every year.
In 1999, President Bill Clinton joined the Jukebox and played saxophone at a halftime show in Grambling.
Mel Blount, Aeneas Williams, and Harold Carmichael — three Pro Football Hall of Famers — all played for the Jaguars.

alumniRoster.achievement: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback who won four Super Bowls as part of the legendary Steel Curtain defense. His physicality changed the rules of how DBs could play. Hall of Fame, 1989.

alumniRoster.name: Aeneas Williams

alumniRoster.achievement: Walk-on at Southern who became one of the greatest defensive backs in NFL history. Played 14 years with the Cardinals and Rams. Hall of Fame, 2014.

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1927 as Houston Colored Junior College to serve Black students barred from the University of Houston, Texas Southern University grew directly out of the landmark Supreme Court case Sweatt v. Painter (1950), which challenged the separate-but-equal doctrine and helped pave the way for Brown v. Board of Education. Located in Houston's historic Third Ward, TSU is the largest HBCU in Texas and home to the Ocean of Soul, one of the most celebrated marching bands in HBCU culture.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as Houston Colored Junior College
Ocean of Soul marching band founded
Football program established
Sweatt v. Painter Supreme Court ruling — TSU alumnus Heman Sweatt's lawsuit helped dismantle segregated higher education

Beyoncé donates $100,000 to the Ocean of Soul marching band

funFacts: Texas Southern exists in part because of Heman Sweatt, whose lawsuit against the University of Texas Law School led to the 1950 Supreme Court ruling that helped end educational segregation.
In 2025, Houston native Beyoncé donated $100,000 to the Ocean of Soul marching band.
The Motion of the Ocean dance line was featured on America's Best Dance Crew.
TSU alumni include Grammy Award-winning jazz saxophonist Kirk Whalum, who was a member of the Ocean of Soul.
TSU's debate team, founded in 1949, trained some of the most prominent civic leaders in American history.

alumniRoster.name: Michael Strahan
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · NFL Sacks Record · TV Host
alumniRoster.achievement: Set the NFL single-season sack record (22.5) in 2001. Won Super Bowl XLII with the Giants. Host of Good Morning America. Hall of Fame, 2014.
alumniRoster.quote: TSU made me the person I am — Houston is in my DNA.

alumniRoster.name: Winston Hill
alumniRoster.role: Pro Football Hall of Fame · 2— Super Bowl Champion OT
alumniRoster.achievement: New York Jets offensive tackle who protected Joe Namath in Super Bowl III. Played 15 NFL seasons. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2020.

alumniRoster.name: Barbara Jordan
alumniRoster.role: U.S. Congresswoman · Civil Rights Champion
alumniRoster.achievement: First Black woman elected to the Texas Senate and later the U.S. House. Her Watergate Committee speech in 1974 is considered one of the greatest in American political history.
alumniRoster.quote: What the people want is very simple — they want an America as good as its promise.

history.briefHistory: Founded in 1875 as Branch Normal College by the Reconstruction-era Arkansas legislature, the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff is the second oldest public institution in the state and the first institution of higher education for Black Arkansans. Known as the Flagship of the Delta, UAPB has been a cornerstone of Black education, culture, and athletics in the Mid-South for 150 years. The M4 marching band, founded in 1946, has grown into one of the most celebrated bands in the SWAC.

historicMilestones.event: Founded as Branch Normal College by the Reconstruction-era Arkansas legislature
Marching Musical Machine of the Mid-South (M4) founded by Miss Alma L. Brown

funFacts: UAPB is the second oldest public institution in Arkansas, founded just two years after the University of Arkansas.
The M4 performed at President Obama's 2009 Inaugural Parade and at the 2025 Honda Battle of the Bands.
UAPB's program in aquaculture and fisheries is one of the most respected in the nation, supporting a $1.2 billion industry in the Mississippi Delta.
L.C. Greenwood — the UAPB's most famous NFL alumni — was a four-time Super Bowl champion and member of Pittsburgh's legendary Steel Curtain defense.
Terron Armstead, one of the NFL's top offensive tackles, played his college ball at UAPB from 2009 to 2012.

alumniRoster.quote: UAPB gave me the foundation. I built the rest.
